content: Question 1. What’s your favourite place in your city to spend time with your male friends? Why - feel free to be specific?

I don’t mind starting point one, uh, my favourite place in my city to spend time with my male friends is the golf course.  Uh, the reason why is  I can just get away from the stresses of my life , um,  I suppose it’s like a journey along with golf.  Yeah, I just feel  a lot more relaxed and free, I guess, when I'm with my friends playing golf.

I’ll go. At the moment, um, it’s probably at the bar, because you watch the Euros at the moment. So it's quite a, it's quite quite a male sort of dominated environment in general.  Um, but then during the winter of play, I play rugby. So it's,  again, it's a sporting type thing where you go out and thrash it out with 29 other guys. So again, it's about that sort of just escaping from sort of the day to day mundane, mundaneness.

Um, actually I don't have any, uh, favourite place. Um, probably comes from the fact that I like to explore new places and I'm looking  for the perfect place, so until like I didn't find that I think we'll go to other places and yeah, that's. To be honest, I don't think I will find one but it's just probably, uh, yeah, I just like to see something different. I did go to places, uh, that I've been before but there's not like the one place I would always go.

I think, um, for me, um, it's similar to Noah and just probably just the pub. Um, there's not really much to do or offer in Swindon to be honest. But um yeah, just going down the pub and just yeah, just have a bit of fun and get away from day to day nine to five  stuff. And particularly you know, whilst the Euros is on it's been quite fun so, um, yeah, just like pub at the weekend or something similar.

On me, I like the coffee shop like we have like Nero, Coffee Nero. We walk to town hall sometimes we gather with friends there and just sitting in with a view and there are some options for drink anything to [unintelligible], I like there I could say.
Question 2. How do you decide what to eat?

Maybe I can start like for eating if I go for, maybe let's say Wetherspoon or somewhere, I firstly check the menu actually if I like something. Um, for me, I don't eat pork. That's why like this is my limitations and other options I just check in what I can eat. In that day if I feel for example want to eat meat or like beef or chicken depends on that I choose  but generally choose chicken I think I'd like that.

I don’t mind going. In terms of what I decide to eat, um, I try to plan my meals. But I guess it's how I’m feeling on the day. Um, I get quite bored if I know I've got something, got something for dinner and I don't want it. Um, I've realised that I won’t eat it and I’ll prepare myself something, anyway, so I don't really plan what to eat, I kind of just decide on the fly while I'm feeling like that day. Um,  because yeah for me, meals are supposed to be enjoyable. So I don't want to eat spaghetti bolognese or something every single day.  So yeah, that's me.

Um, I um obviously um, if we talk about like, um, like a relaxing day, um, I will try to find something  that I  like would say like, my comfort zone. So, uh, comfort food, rather. And uh I will, yeah, I will have it.  Then if I eat outside, like with friends, it's uh about I think accommodating everyone.  Um, it depends on the type of friends that are with me or if like we're going for kind of snacks or we're like going for proper  uh dinner, for example. But it's, um, I don't really eat out on my own really, but um if I ate at home, like it will be something that is a comfort food. And not too complicated to make. Because I'm I like to make like food that is easy to make but tastes good. But I'm not a huge fan of the process of cooking.  Um, so yeah.

I would say I'm probably quite impulsive when it comes to choosing what to eat.  I don't really think about it too much. It's just, um, I would go to the supermarket maybe pick up an array of things and then sort of create into whatever  during the week there. If I don't fancy whatever is in the house I just go out and get something different. There's no real deciding. It's kind of like it's more, um, to describe it, it's like  it's just kind of existing. It’s not like a big decision goes in. It's just like whatever is happening on the day.  It's quite fluid.

Yeah, similar to me really. Um, so I do like a monthly food shop. Um,  I live on my own so  I sort of have that for the month and then choose within that month's worth of food but then similar to um to you guys if I don't  if I know I've got something that evening but then I don't fancy it, I'll just go out and  if I'm eating out just depends on what's on the menu to be honest and what I fancy there and then.
Question 3. Do you think your gender influences what you eat? Tell us more about why or why not?

I don't think gender influences what I eat at all. Um,  like if there's something I want I'll just have it . There's no such thing as a manly or womanly dish if you ask me, it's just like, it's just food. And like,  so it's literally got zero influence  on whether I'd eat something or not.
Yeah I don't think as well like rather than what you eat maybe I can say size can  affect sometimes, maybe I can eat more. Rather than female difference.
Yeah I don't look at, um, I don't I don't know what's, uh, like a female meal or male meal. I just eat what I like.  And yeah, maybe like Bilal says, maybe about portions, but nothing in particular.
I agree that gender doesn't play any role whatsoever, um,  in regards to what I eat.  Yeah there's no manly or womanly food. Food is food and yeah, yeah.  Doesn't influence me whatsoever.

Yeah, same with me. I've never even thought about it until I read that question, to be honest. I didn't know, I don't know if it's even a thing but um, I just, if I like it, or if I want it, I'll have it. And that's it really. That's literally the only factor that comes into it. And if it's at a restaurant, I suppose it's, uh,  if I can afford it, it's, you know, an expensive place, but um  yeah, most of the time, it’s just, do I want it? Okay, let's have it .
Question 4. Imagine you decided to go plant-based - what would need to change in your life for you to do that?

Yeah, so I couldn't imagine myself going on a plant based diet at all.  Like  I've had to think of what I've actually ate for breakfast this morning. I actually just ate four sausages by themselves. Not exactly the healthiest start to the day,  but I just couldn't imagine going entirely plant based.
And even if,  do you know one of the things that really annoys me about, um, the plant based alternatives at the moment, is they advertise themselves as like cauliflower steak and like, but you're not a steak. You're not even close to what a steak is. You're something,  you’re something else entirely. Um, so, the reason to like actually go plant based,  I think they'd need to like stop lying, because I feel like it's a lie to really call something a cauliflower steak.  So I feel like they need to get their own terms  of what it is, and then I could accept  the product a bit more.
Uh, but there’d need to be like  I probably need to give up meat. But that's just not going to happen.

Yeah, no, I agree. I think, for instance, yeah, like plant based sausages,  why are they being plant based sausages? I thought the whole  reason was to be meat free, is to, is to not be meat. So why would you manufacture it and make it look like something that is meat? Isn't the whole point of the principle of your  plant based, I suppose, the movement, that is anti, is anti meat? So why are you trying to make it look like meat, if that makes sense? If you do something that was, I don't know, anti-birth,  you wouldn't then make something that looks just like a person, would you? That's a very poor example, but the point I'm trying to make is, yeah, don't call it plant based sausages. Call it something else.  It’s not, it’s not a sausage.

Yeah, I agree, um, on my side. Um, I am not a plant based eater. And uh  I may have tried once. Um, I was never really satisfied. Uh, but yeah, like uh, I don't like the. Yeah, for me, it's a lie. Or like  cheese, like plant based cheese. If you look at a definition of cheese, this is something that's got milk. So you can't call something that doesn't have milk,  uh, cheese, you know. And that kind of pulled me,  pulled me away from trying, because I feel like I'm trying to be something but it's not, it's not real. And it doesn't go well with me. So uh just for that reason, and also, it's a bit more expensive. Um, it's a bit more difficult to get, I think. So, um, I don't want to  I don't want it to be too complicated. And we should, like whoever eats  plant based should uh just accept it's fine. Some people eat meat or whatever. And uh we should be okay with, call it, like, something different. Not saying it's cheese, but saying it's whatever it should be called. Yeah.

Yeah, I think cost is a massive factor as well. It's also expensive, and especially now, cost of living crisis,  et cetera. I mean I’d love to  eat organic food and  look after the environment, but  kind of need to survive. So unfortunately, yeah, just can’t do it.

Do you know one of the other things that actually puts me off as well, is you don't actually really know what type of product you're getting. So let's say it's called, like, a bean burger. Like the variance between,  like, you know what a beef burger is exactly right, you just know. Whereas if it's a bean burger, it's like, well, what beans have you put into this? Is it black beans, is it kidney beans? Like I'm actually gonna have to sit and read the label here  to see what this is going to be about. Whereas  if it's a beef burger, I just know that that’s, like how that's going to [unintelligible] and roughly know how that's going to taste.  Um, so I think  like, they need to be much more descriptive as to what's actually going in  to this product so I know what I'm going to be getting.

Yeah, I think, um, yes, it's something that's  that's doesn't like, crossed my radar too much. And I agree because there's obviously a lot of, um,  you know, um , what do you call it, like,  processed foods and stuff gets a lot of flack. But then you know, if you think about stuff like plant based cheese, it's like how on earth did you even make that? Like, I don't know I don't understand the processes of manufacturing like to the finer details but do you take the plant and turn it into cheese? Like surely that must be processed in some really odd way but yeah, um, sort of go on to point five a bit is that if you could get like burgers and sausages that are plant based and they tasted exactly like beef and they cost exactly the same as beef then I'd consider it, but they're a long way off from that at the moment.

Yeah, I agree. But in some point, sometimes  it helps make actually like for example, if I follow halal diet because I am Muslim,  sometimes plant based foods having good choice for me when I go to a non-halal place. Like, it is the easy option for me and just choosing them.  Yeah maybe name can be different and they can show how the manufacturing process and they can say different things, as you said.
Question 5. What might make plant-based foods more appealing to you or other men you know?

I think maybe if we, if we know how clear the processing like if you know what ingredients, like, very well, even maybe it's showing with a kind of pictures instead of writing just typing, because some of them maybe we don't know what what ingredient what's it's like how the process. Maybe it can be, like, if it's tested, I would like to try more maybe.

I think yeah, a bit more transparency on what's in there. That’d certainly make it more appealing to me. Certainly, considering cost. I also think, is the  is the, is is stop trying to make me feel bad because I'm eating meat. As human beings it's what we've been doing for 1000s of years, so, whilst yes they may have their reasons, it’s almost, these people almost, they almost think they're holier  than holy, because they eat plant based foods.
And it’s like, we’re all different. I'm sure there's certain elements of their life that  I'd perhaps disagree with. I'm sure if I found that out I wouldn't just hammer on them every time they did that. Or. Just yeah.  I just think we're all individuals. And let's just keep it that way. And some people like plant based foods, some don't, but don't make me feel bad about the decisions I'm making in my life because  life's hard as it is, let alone having people  give me a bit of a bullying because of the type of food you eat.

Yeah, um,  for me, one big thing is like, um,  like the brands or whoever needs to accept that it’s a different kind of meal, meals, sorry, and, uh, not trying to pretend to be  like what you avoid, like, cheese. Like it's not cheese, but just give it another name. I don't, I don't have an example. But just to accept it.  Um, because I don't want to, it makes me feel like, like I'm,  I'm lying to myself, pretending oh, I'm eating something that tastes like milk. But it’s not milk. You know, like. So yeah, just to be like to accept it is a different type of  food, and they are different type of food and we already accept it. But that should be another one here. And it’s all fine. And, um,  I'm sure more people will be interested eventually.

I'm not actually sure  anything could be done to make plant based foods more appealing to me because  I've must have,  I'm just thinking, like, whenever you go out for a Sunday roast, or whatever, like 95% of your plate is plant based. It's just like the roast beef or the roast chicken, whatever it is, you have. Like,  I actually don't want to give that up full stop. There's potatoes, carrots, whatever else happens to be on that plate most of the time. But to me the mix is actually quite important. Like I really want that versus the other stuff to be honest. So I don't think there is anything that's gonna make me switch.
Like the only thing that's gonna stop me from consuming meat,  is if the government turn around and put the tax way up on it, and it becomes unaffordable.  But even then it's going to be, I’m probably still going to do my best to go and get it anyway. So  I guess the cost of meat is actually what would make plant based foods more appealing. But it’s gonna have to, it would have to become extortionately expensive  for me to change.
And what about uh, like, plant based, like meat being very, very, very cheap,  would it, like, attract you?

No . Just no. Like if it tasted exactly the same and had the same texture,  then it might,  it might work. It's all about taste and texture, though.  Like the texture is the really important part. Um,  because it's,  I don't know, if you ever had chicken where someone's not, like, cooked it the entire way through. It's kind of raw in the middle. You get that, like, rubbery thing. I can't eat that. Like your brain is quite hard wired in these things where it's sort of like, texture is really really important. And so if you’re gonna make it taste like chicken, which is probably quite easy, because everything tastes like chicken,  then can't get that texture correct as well. I think that'll be quite important for me.
